summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly where data lives, eliminating the need to move data to separate ML systems. Capabilities range from in-database model training (SQL-based ML) to native vector search for semantic retrieval and direct LLM integration via serverless inference functions. Gartner projects that by 2026, 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI applications (up from ~2% in 2023), and the vector database market is forecast to reach USD 17.91 billion by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI — serverless LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst, and ML functions
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex provides fully managed, serverless access to LLMs (e.g., from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and others) and task-specific functions like SENTIMENT, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, COMPLETE, and EMBED_TEXT, all callable via SQL or Python. Cortex Search delivers hybrid (vector + keyword) retrieval, and Cortex Analyst enables natural-language-to-SQL. These capabilities now extend to Snowflake Postgres, allowing Cortex AI functions to run against Postgres-managed data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake offers a built-in VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), plus Cortex Search as a managed hybrid vector/keyword retrieval service.
databases.llm_integration: Native, first-party. Hosted LLMs accessible directly via Cortex functions (COMPLETE, EMBED_TEXT) in SQL/Python with no external API keys required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens processed or compute consumed per Cortex function; standard Snowflake storage and warehouse compute apply separately.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML (in-database model training) + Vertex AI / Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, matrix factorization, and more) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call hosted foundation models (including Gemini) through functions like ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, enabling generative AI and embeddings directly in SQL queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports the VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings stored in tables.
databases.llm_integration: Native via Vertex AI remote models; Gemini and other foundation models are invoked through SQL functions over a BigQuery connection to Vertex AI.
databases.pricing_notes: Pay-per-query (on-demand by bytes scanned) or capacity-based slots; BigQuery ML has separate charges for model creation/training and inference; Vertex AI foundation model calls are billed by Vertex AI usage.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for embeddings + pgai for in-database LLM/embedding workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds a vector data type and similarity operators for storing and querying embeddings, while pgai (from Timescale) and related tools automate embedding generation and allow calling LLM providers (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL. This keeps vectors alongside relational data in a single, familiar open-source database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL. Vector search is provided by the third-party pgvector extension (supporting HNSW and IVFFlat indexes); it is not part of the base PostgreSQL engine, though it is widely available on managed Postgres offerings.
databases.llm_integration: Via extensions (pgai, pg_vectorize) that wrap external LLM/embedding provider APIs; not built into core Postgres.
databases.pricing_notes: PostgreSQL itself is free and open-source; costs come from hosting/compute and any external LLM API calls. Managed providers add their own compute/storage pricing.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL-based integration with Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you add ML-based predictions to applications using SQL by invoking Amazon SageMaker endpoints, Amazon Comprehend (for sentiment/NLP), and Amazon Bedrock foundation models directly from queries. This enables inference (predictions, text generation, embeddings) within a transactional Aurora MySQL/PostgreSQL database without building custom integration code.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided via the pgvector extension (a third-party extension), not a built-in Aurora ML feature.
databases.llm_integration: Native SQL integration with Amazon Bedrock (hosted LLMs/embeddings) and SageMaker/Comprehend endpoints via Aurora ML functions.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora compute/storage/I-O plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage charges.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL with Amazon SageMaker and Bedrock
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts and scientists to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL CREATE MODEL statements, with SageMaker Autopilot handling model selection and training behind the scenes. It also supports bring-your-own-model and invoking Amazon Bedrock LLMs and SageMaker endpoints directly from SQL for generative AI and prediction within the data warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Redshift ML focuses on predictive ML and LLM invocation, not vector similarity search; there is no built-in vector index/search type comparable to dedicated vector databases.
databases.llm_integration: Native SQL integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker endpoints invoked from Redshift queries.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra cost for the Redshift ML feature; charges apply for Redshift compute/storage, SageMaker training and inference resources used, and any Bedrock model usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, foundation model APIs, agents) + Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides an end-to-end platform for building, fine-tuning, serving, and governing ML and generative AI models, including Foundation Model APIs, model serving, agent frameworks, and ML lifecycle tooling (MLflow, Unity Catalog governance). Databricks Vector Search is a managed, serverless vector database integrated with the Lakehouse for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a built-in, managed vector database with automatic sync from Delta tables and support for approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Native. Foundation Model APIs provide hosted and pay-per-token access to open and proprietary LLMs; external models can also be served and governed through Mosaic AI Model Serving.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search, Model Serving, and Foundation Model APIs are billed separately (e.g., pay-per-token or provisioned throughput), plus underlying cloud compute/storage.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector search integrated with document data
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables storing embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and running semantic/similarity queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage with HNSW indexing. It is designed for RAG and AI applications, integrating with embedding providers and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex, so AI features can run against live operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Atlas Vector Search is a built-in capability of MongoDB Atlas, providing a dedicated vector index type and the $vectorSearch query stage (no separate vector database required).
databases.llm_integration: No first-party hosted LLM; integrates with external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, etc.) and AI frameworks. LLM calls occur outside the database.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes or shared cluster resources, billed as part of Atlas cluster compute/storage consumption.
